tasks.description: Port compile-dendry.js from Flyt as a runtime-neutral parameterised CLI with its tests: the title fallback, the input and output roots and the one-subgame-per-subdirectory convention become parameters, and the output is byte-identical under Node, Bun and Deno
tasks.notes: Was Flyt 10IC.5. Flyt's ADR 0002 (Flyt PR #30, branch docs/adr-compiler-home) is the brief and records the evidence. Runtime-neutral means: import built-ins with the node: prefix (node:fs, node:path), sort every directory listing before use, use no API only one runtime has and pin no behaviour to a runtime. Flyt measured the existing script (imports only fs and path) unchanged under Node 25.2.1, Bun 1.3.5 and Deno 2.9.7: all exit cleanly, but Bun lists directories in a different order from Node and the compiler inserts scenes in read order, so great-hall.json has the same 94 scenes in a different order under Bun. Acceptance: a fixture story compiled under all three runtimes with the outputs compared; if CI cannot install all three, record which it covers and which is checked by hand. Acceptance also includes the engine vocabulary guard covering the compiler, so the CLI must live under the guard's path filter (currently src/lib/) or the filter must widen with it

tasks.description: Keep the compiler CLI behind its own export path so browser bundles never import file system code
tasks.notes: Review note carried from Flyt PR #30. The constraint is file system code out of the browser bundle; the CLI itself stays runtime-neutral (1CC.1)

tasks.description: Write the .dry format reference doc, moved from Flyt's docs/dendrynexus-reference.md, and document how to run the compiler CLI under Node, Bun and Deno
tasks.notes: Describes the compiler's input format, so it moves with the compiler. Also resolves the doc-comment references Flyt 8EX.5 removed for want of a Riffle equivalent. The package bin entry carries the usual node shebang because npm expects it; Bun users run it with bunx --bun and Deno users with deno run --allow-read --allow-write (commands as Flyt ran them; re-check against the shipped CLI before documenting)
Flyt then bumps the dependency, switches its compile:dendry script to the CLI and retires scripts/compile-dendry.js (Flyt-side tasks)

tasks.description: Copy ADR 0001 (the Riffle boundary rule) and ADR 0002 (the compiler's home) from Flyt's docs/adr/ into Riffle's docs/adr/
tasks.notes: Both govern this repo but live only in Flyt. Flyt keeps ADR 0001 as the decision record of origin with a pointer here. Copy the updated ADR 0002 (it records the runtime-neutral requirement), found on Flyt PR #30's branch docs/adr-compiler-home, not the earlier text

tasks.description: Document reset() in the README, and decide whether evaluateCondition is public API (a README row) or internal (marked so in the types)
tasks.notes: From Flyt, found while fixing a review comment on Flyt PR #29: Flyt's CLAUDE.md now defers to this README for the engine API. reset() clears the loaded game and state and returns loading and error to their defaults (Flyt calls it when the player returns to the menu); restart() returns to the first scene of the same game, and is the only one the README mentions. The 1.1.0 type declarations also expose evaluateCondition(condition?: string): boolean (src/lib/engine.svelte.ts:797), which the README omits. Changelog entry goes under Unreleased; ship as a 1.1.x patch or fold into the next release
